html:
The August Revolution was the seizure of power across Vietnam by the Viet Minh in the last weeks of August 1945, as Japan surrendered at the end of the Second World War.

Japan had removed the French in March 1945 and left a weak puppet government. In the north a famine had killed perhaps a million people. As Japan gave up, the Viet Minh, led by communists, took Hanoi on 19 August, then Huế and Saigon. Emperor Bảo Đại abdicated, ending the Nguyễn dynasty of Gia Long.

On 2 September 1945, in Ba Đình Square in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh read a declaration of independence that opened with words from the American one. The French returned to the south within weeks, and the First Indochina War began in 1946.
sum: The August Revolution was the seizure of power across Vietnam by the Viet Minh in the last weeks of August 1945, as Japan surrendered at the end of the Second World War.
